quest.title: Towards the Lighthouse, or Far Away
quest.description: Something seems to be troubling someone in the collapsed lighthouse outside Brickstacks...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x350, Primogem x40, Mora x30000, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x4

dialogues.speaker: Esnoir
dialogues.text: How about... We tear it down brick by brick and rebuild a new tower from scratch?

dialogues.speaker: Esnoir
dialogues.text: Hmm, no, no... That could send <color=#00E1FFFF>the lamp atop the tower</color> rolling right down...

dialogues.speaker: Esnoir
dialogues.text: Dear guests, you've returned.

choices.text: Why are you still guarding the lighthouse?

response.speaker: Esnoir
response.text: Well, he is the first place venturers come to upon returning to the village.

response.speaker: Esnoir
response.text: Yes, he has collapsed, but I must do all I can to sort things out here. I cannot allow him to receive our returnees all by his lonesome.

response.speaker: Esnoir
response.text: And then there's Rozel. He has been drifting so far from home for so long — I absolutely must give him a hug the moment he returns!

response.speaker: Esnoir
response.text: So please, help me, dear guests — I will be here waiting for him, and for you too!

choices.text: Tell me, what are venturers again?

response.speaker: Esnoir
response.text: Venturers are explorers and wayfarers. They are those who are willing to leave everything behind and travel far abroad.

response.speaker: Esnoir
response.text: The distant places they wish to venture to include the far edge of starfalls, the other side of the rainbow.

response.speaker: Esnoir
response.text: And when they wish to return, this lighthouse is their only guide.

response.speaker: Esnoir
response.text: Traveling abroad is a good thing, of this there is no doubt. Yet there are some venturers who return from their travels changed.

response.speaker: Esnoir
response.text: Some mumble constantly about "value," and when they see a beautiful hat, they immediately ask how much it costs and what materials it's made from...

response.speaker: Esnoir
response.text: It's almost as if they cannot see the flower in that hat or the beautiful patterns woven into it.

response.speaker: Esnoir
response.text: Rozel says that it is because the many things venturers have seen color them, like ponds into which paint has been thrown.

response.speaker: Esnoir
response.text: I asked if it was a good or a bad thing, but he merely called it change — and that change is neither good nor bad.

response.speaker: Esnoir
response.text: I must confess that I simply do not understand...

choices.text: Mind telling me more about Rozel?

response.speaker: Esnoir
response.text: Rozel was my neighbor. We'd chat, have tea, and play games together every day.

response.speaker: Esnoir
response.text: But one day, he told me that he wished to become a venturer, and soon, he began his travels.

response.speaker: Esnoir
response.text: First, he traveled the entire world, going to Constellation Metropole, Rainsong Pond, and the Forest of Blessings.

response.speaker: Esnoir
response.text: After that, he wanted to go still further abroad. So he built himself a little boat, planning to set sail for the far edge, where the stars fall.

response.speaker: Esnoir
response.text: He asked me to journey with him, but... I did not board. All I did was make him a windmill.

response.speaker: Esnoir
response.text: That way, he would at least sail faster while out at sea, and thus when it came time to return, his would be all the more swift.

response.speaker: Esnoir
response.text: Right! Rozel is unlike other venturers. He knows how to wear a hat and the reason why houses exist.

choices.text: See you.

response.speaker: Esnoir
response.text: See you, honored guests! I shall be here waiting for Rozel, and for you.

dialogues.speaker: Esnoir
dialogues.text: Lighthouse... Lighthouse... I've got to haul you up, so my friends can find the way home... Phew... Just got to rest a bit before I do...

choices.text: This isn't something a human can just pull into place.

response.speaker: Esnoir
response.text: Hmm? What ho, you don't look like one of our neighbors from Brickstacks. A rarity indeed!

response.speaker: Esnoir
response.text: Esnoir's the name, and guarding this here Farseer Lighthouse's the game. It and I bid you welcome.

response.speaker: Esnoir
response.text: In truth, however, you've come at a most terrible time. T'was but a few scant moments ago when a monstrous dragon just ran by in a right hurry.

response.speaker: Esnoir
response.text: Clumsy and stumbling it was, and the two of us were in its wrathful path.

response.speaker: Esnoir
response.text: With a crack and a snap, both I and my poor lighthouse were bowled right over... And as you can see, I've regained my footing, but not so the lighthouse.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh... You sure are making light of that lighthouse being knocked down by that giant dragon, aren't you?

response.speaker: Esnoir
response.text: Aye, and I've tried all manner of ways to get him on his feet. Even the neighbors came to lend a hand.

response.speaker: Esnoir
response.text: But he simply refused to stand back up again. You'd almost think he had a temper, to throw such a tantrum...

response.speaker: Esnoir
response.text: Our neighbors still have to keep an eye on that dragon, so I'm on my own for the time being.

response.speaker: Esnoir
response.text: Agh! This is a terrible situation. With our lighthouse down for the count, we'll have no light... That means no return to the village for our venturers!

choices.text: Wait. What are "venturers"?

response.speaker: Esnoir
response.text: Why, explorers, wayfarers. Those willing to leave everything behind and travel far abroad.

response.speaker: Esnoir
response.text: Their journeys take them to the ends of the skies. After all, a mere jaunt over to Constellation Metropole or Rainsong Pond requires no lighthouse to show the way.

response.speaker: Esnoir
response.text: And so venturers board their little boats and set sail for where the stars set — or perhaps the other end of the rainbow.

response.speaker: Esnoir
response.text: When they wish to return, this lighthouse shall be their guide.

response.speaker: Esnoir
response.text: When they return, some venturers have grown most strange, mumbling ceaselessly about "value" and "suitability."

response.speaker: Esnoir
response.text: But that doesn't stop their luggage from containing many pretty stones, beautiful art, and seeds!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Wait, and what if they don't wish to return?

response.speaker: Esnoir
response.text: Why, that is their prerogative! But no matter what, the radiance of the Brickstacks Lighthouse shall shine upon the distant places where the stars fall.

response.speaker: Esnoir
response.text: So long as they are willing, anyone may follow that light back to our village at any time.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Where the stars fall... That almost sounds like you're trying to go explore beyond this world...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #So that's... Eh? {NICKNAME}? What's with that frown?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I wonder what becomes of them once they depart...

response.speaker: Esnoir
response.text: I am no venturer, so I know not. Were Rozel still here, you could have asked him.

response.speaker: Esnoir
response.text: He is the boldest, most inquisitive of our venturers. By dint of the windmill mounted on his ship, he sojourns to places most distant each time — to lands where even the light may fail, and yet, he always returns.

response.speaker: Esnoir
response.text: According to the plan he related it to me, he should have already returned several days ago. I fear he may have utterly lost his way, like my other wayfaring neighbors...

response.speaker: Esnoir
response.text: Alright! I've rested enough. Now is the time to get our lighthouse back on its feet to shine once more! All our venturers await its guiding radiance to bring them home, after all!

response.speaker: Esnoir
response.text: Dear guest, could I please seek your aid in getting our lighthouse back on his feet? That way, his light can shine further still, that it may be seen by more of our venturers.

choices.text: Don't worry, I'll get it done right this instant.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, are you sure about that!? P—Paimon's not that strong, so... She'll cheer for you while you're at it!

response.speaker: Esnoir
response.text: Haha... Does seem a right pickle, doesn't it? Why don't we put our heads together and think of something... Hmm, how about... we tear it down brick by brick, and rebuild it from scratch?

response.speaker: Esnoir
response.text: No, no. The hook that hung the lamp up has been knocked loose. Just one moment of carelessness... Who knows, it could send <color=#00E1FFFF>the lamp</color> rolling down...

choices.text: I'm just gonna check out the environs a bit first, don't mind me...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, even if we had the tools...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Is it even possible to right it? The lighthouse is so huge...

choices.text: And where would they travel "abroad"?
Seems like you're going to need my help.

dialogues.speaker: Elegant Statue
dialogues.text: (Here, make the <color=#00E1FFFF>wish</color> you hold so dear, and the reasons for your prayer you must make clear.)

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: As Paimon cheers you on, you firmly support the lighthouse with your shoulder, plant your feet firmly, and...\nHeave ho!\n

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: The toppled tower salutes you stoically (and statically) with its weighty body — if nothing else, you courageously confronted this challenge.\nHeave ho, hup!\n

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: The lighthouse lies resolutely on the ground, silently extending its beneficence to you.\n

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Heave ho— Ack!\nA dull crack sounds from near your hip, and you fall to the floor. It is only after lengthy and gentle ministrations on Paimon's part that you are again able to rise...\n

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Best you think of some other way to do this...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: After giving much thought as to where your strength would be best applied, you select a brick that seems like a firm handhold.\nGrabbing onto it, and to the sound of Paimon's cheers, you let loose a burst of tremendous effort to right the toppled tower...\n

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: ...Only to nearly be sent, friendly handhold-brick and all, tumbling off the island. Fortunately, Paimon manages to grab onto your clothes.\n

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You... should probably consider an alternative...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text:
As Paimon cheers you on, you settle into a steady stance and tighten up your core, both hands grabbing onto the section of the toppled lighthouse best suited for gripping.
Adjust the distance... Breathe in... Stick out your chest... Put your strength into your shoulders... Wait, should it be your shoulders or your back?
Well, whatever the case, time to put your back and/or shoulders into it! Heave ho!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: ...As Paimon comforts you and the lighthouse looks on, you let go for now.\n

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Just... think of something else already, would you...

talks.objective: Find a way to make the lighthouse... stand up?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! The lamp really came off! I—It isn't broken now, is it?

choices.text: C—Calm down, Paimon! It's still glowing!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh? Huh. You're right. But why is it still shining even after being removed?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Never mind that for now. Let's put the lamp back before anyone sees us!

response.speaker: Esnoir
response.text: Please wait, honored guests!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh oh, uh oh, this has gotta be the lightkeeper!

choices.text: L—Look, the lamp's still glowing...

response.speaker: Esnoir
response.text: No, no, of course not. If anything, dear guests, you've saved me much time and trouble by bringing it down!

response.speaker: Esnoir
response.text: Ah, yes. I've forgotten to introduce myself. Esnoir is my name, and I am the lighthouse keeper. This here is said lighthouse — and I greet you on both our behalves.

response.speaker: Esnoir
response.text: Still, this is a bad time. A while ago, our lighthouse here was felled by a fuming, furious dragon... I'm still trying to figure out how to lift him up again.

response.speaker: Esnoir
response.text: That way, his light shall shine upon even the most distant of places, that our wayfaring venturers may find their way back to our village.

response.speaker: Esnoir
response.text: That said, since you've retrieved this lamp, I'm thinking that... if you could mount it somewhere high, its light should be visible even to distant venturers.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh... That makes sense to Paimon!

choices.text: Let's back up a bit, shall we? What are "venturers," again?

response.speaker: Esnoir
response.text: Ah. You two must be new here. They are explorers, wayfarers — those willing to leave everything behind and travel far abroad.

response.speaker: Esnoir
response.text: Their journeys take them to the ends of the skies. After all, a mere jaunt over to Constellation Metropole or Rainsong Pond requires no lighthouse to show the way.

response.speaker: Esnoir
response.text: And so venturers board their little boats and set sail for where the stars set — or perhaps the other end of the rainbow.

response.speaker: Esnoir
response.text: When they wish to return, this lighthouse shall be their guide.

response.speaker: Esnoir
response.text: When they return, some venturers have grown most strange, mumbling ceaselessly about "value" and "suitability."

response.speaker: Esnoir
response.text: But that doesn't stop their luggage from containing many pretty stones, beautiful art, and seeds!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Wait, and what if they don't wish to return?

response.speaker: Esnoir
response.text: Why, that is their prerogative! No matter what, the radiance of the Brickstacks Lighthouse shall shine upon the distant places where the stars fall.

response.speaker: Esnoir
response.text: So long as they are willing, anyone may follow that light back to our village at any time. But now that the lighthouse has fallen, his lamplight cannot cross those vast distances...

response.speaker: Esnoir
response.text: My friend, Rozel, just set off a few days ago. He must surely have gotten utterly lost now, just like all our other venturers.

response.speaker: Esnoir
response.text: I wish to set this lighthouse back up. But he remains unmoving, even with the entire village working together. But now... You've managed to take down the lamp.

choices.text: If this lamp remains lit even after being removed...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh... You're right! If we do that, the lamp's light will definitely be visible, even at a distance.

choices.text: If only there were hooks in the sky to hang it on...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's just like when we hung up stars with Navia. It's just a shame that we don't have the Aerial Express with us this time...

response.speaker: Esnoir
response.text: And as it happens, I do know of an island — the highest point in the area. Rozel taught me how to survey elevation, and I've already estimated the elevation of all the nearby isles in his absence... You know, to pass the time.

response.speaker: Esnoir
response.text: If we hung the lamp up there, the light would be visible from far away for sure. That should be enough to allow our venturers to find their way back home.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That said, this Rozel guy sure knows a lot...

response.speaker: Esnoir
response.text: Of course. Rozel is the bravest, most inquisitive venturer we have. Not only has he traveled the length and breadth of the world, but he has traveled still further beyond our world on his windmill ship...

response.speaker: Esnoir
response.text: He often ranges far abroad indeed, even to places where the lamp-light fails to touch. But he's told me that no matter how weak the lamp's light is, he always knows where the lighthouse is, and can follow it back to the village.

choices.text: Let's go have a look at that island, shall we?

response.speaker: Esnoir
response.text: I—I would love to go... But I must stay and keep watch over the lighthouse, for it is the first place venturers come upon returning to the village.

response.speaker: Esnoir
response.text: Yes, he has collapsed, but I must do all I can to sort things out here. I cannot allow him to receive our returnees all by his lonesome.

response.speaker: Esnoir
response.text: And then there's Rozel. He has been drifting so far from home for so long — I absolutely must give him a hug the moment he returns!

response.speaker: Esnoir
response.text: So please, dear guests! Could you help me hang up the lamp at the highest point possible? I have some savings — your deed shall not go unrewarded.

choices.text: Rozel's that awesome, huh?

response.speaker: Esnoir
response.text: Of course! He will not sit around and wait for death — his heart is far too stout for that!

response.speaker: Esnoir
response.text: Even should the lamp's light fail utterly, he would use his windmill to seek hither and thither for the way back to our village.

response.speaker: Esnoir
response.text: So please help me, dear guests — and Rozel, too.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Well, at this point, we're not going to say no.

response.speaker: Esnoir
response.text: Thank you, thank you! My gratitude and more — on behalf of my lighthouse, and Rozel too!

response.speaker: Esnoir
response.text: I shall be here waiting for him, and for you.

choices.text: Don't worry. Leave this to me.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What? Hey! Don't just give it to Paimon! Someone's definitely watching this thing — they're gonna rake us over the coals for sure!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, what do we do now... Huh? Wait a minute. Why is this lamp still shining, even after being removed?

choices.text: C—Calm down, Paimon! It's still glowing!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So the reason the lighthouse shone so brightly is that there was a super bright "light" hanging in the lighthouse...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That said, aren't light sources usually super complex mechanisms?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh, that's not important! Since this one can be removed normally, that works for us!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Esnoir mentioned earlier that he needs to get the lighthouse standing back up again because he wants to put the light someplace high so more people can see it...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: In that case, let's just hang it up somewhere high, right now!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe, that's what Paimon was thinking too! ...Y'know, wouldn't everyone be able to see it if we could hang it up in the sky?

choices.text: If only there were hooks in the sky to hang it on...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's just like when we hung up stars with Navia. It's just a shame that we don't have the Aerial Express with us this time...

response.speaker: Esnoir
response.text: Hahaha, that's not a bad idea at all!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: O—Oh, uh, hey there, Esnoir! We didn't break... anything... did we?

choices.text: L—Look, the lamp's still glowing...

response.speaker: Esnoir
response.text: Why, certainly! If it glows still, it fits the bill.

response.speaker: Esnoir
response.text: And indeed, you spoke true earlier as well. If we could find a place higher than the lighthouse upon which to mount this lamp, then its light would be all the clearer to see from further away.

response.speaker: Esnoir
response.text: And as it happens, I do know of an island — the highest point in the area. Rozel taught me how to survey elevation, and I've already estimated the elevation of all the nearby isles in his absence... You know, to pass the time.

response.speaker: Esnoir
response.text: If we hung the lamp up there, the light would be visible from far away for sure. That should be enough to allow our venturers to find their way back home.

choices.text: Well, there we go. A solution to our problem.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe. No way a simple problem like this could stump us!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That said, this Rozel guy sure knows a lot...

response.text: But now, the lighthouse has collapsed, and the lamp's light has fallen beneath the horizon...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: This tree proves surprisingly amenable to ornaments of the lamp variety, and you have it hung up in no time.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That should do it! The light should shine far and wide now.

choices.text: Not that anything's happened yet.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We wait, of course! Maybe those venturers have seen the light already, and are on the way back as we speak.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh... Nothing's happened. Not a person has returned.

response.speaker: Panuelle
response.text: Hello, you two. Not to disturb you or anything, but what were you intending to do by hanging that light up again?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Well, long story short...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You tell Panuelle what happened...

response.speaker: Panuelle
response.text: I see. I've heard about the issue with Esnoir and the lighthouse as well, and this idea is a good one. However...

choices.text: Perhaps we could hang it up still higher.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, it's not like we can literally hang it up in the sky, can we?

response.speaker: Panuelle
response.text: Hanging the lamp up in the sky... That could, perhaps, be possible.

choices.text: See? Told you there was a way!

response.speaker: Panuelle
response.text: Please, let me finish! This idea of mine may not actually work...

response.speaker: Panuelle
response.text: The Whispering Isle is not far from here. If a gift is offered unto the goddess on that island, she will grant the supplicant their wish...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Woah, that's some island!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Righto! So, let's take this lamp on over to that Whispering Isle and see what the deal is!

response.speaker: Panuelle
response.text: That said, I do not know if that goddess still hears our wishes...

response.speaker: Panuelle
response.text: I've been to that island to offer gifts, but my wishes were not granted. Perhaps something's gone wrong somewhere...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Eh? What did you wish for?

response.speaker: Panuelle
response.text: My wish was a simple one — to be friends with Chauvigne forever...

response.speaker: Panuelle
response.text: We used to live here together, taking care of this tree, drinking tea, and chatting...

response.speaker: Panuelle
response.text: He once set off on a long journey, and when he returned, he was almost unrecognizable. Not that it should've mattered! We were still friends, I thought. We'd understand one another!

response.speaker: Panuelle
response.text: But he grew stranger and stranger, his days filled with odd mumblings and melancholy... He even rejected all my tea party invitations!

response.speaker: Panuelle
response.text: I feared that he might no longer want to be my friend, so I made plans to go to the Whispering Isle and make a wish to the goddess.

response.speaker: Panuelle
response.text: The oldest legend in our village says that originally, the goddess greatly favored the brave. So long as a valiant person were to bring her a gift as proof of their courage, she would respond to them...

response.speaker: Panuelle
response.text: But... I feared that she would not bestow her favor upon me, and so I brought a dragon scale with me.

response.speaker: Panuelle
response.text: Do you know about the giant dragon that suddenly emerged from the toytanium mines?

response.speaker: Panuelle
response.text: It flattened a great many homes and even mashed that mountain... Now, our venturers can no longer repair their boats or make tools there, and have had to change from whence they embark on their adventures...

response.speaker: Panuelle
response.text: That mountain is just over there, but nowadays, he's as broken as the Broken Sea itself.

response.speaker: Panuelle
response.text: We've constantly tried to chase the dragon away and defend our village!

response.speaker: Panuelle
response.text: Whenever it flew above our village, we would grab chairs, tables, forks, and spoons with which to chase it away.

response.text: We used to live here together, taking care of this tree, drinking tea, and chatting...

response.speaker: Panuelle
response.text: He once set off on a long journey, and when he returned, he was almost unrecognizable. Not that it should've mattered! We were still friends, I thought. We'd understand one another!

response.speaker: Panuelle
response.text: But he grew stranger and stranger, his days filled with odd mumblings and melancholy... He even rejected all my tea party invitations!

response.speaker: Panuelle
response.text: I feared that he might no longer want to be my friend, so I made plans to go to the Whispering Isle and make a wish to the goddess.

response.speaker: Panuelle
response.text: The oldest legend in our village says that originally, the goddess greatly favored the brave. So long as a valiant person were to bring her a gift as proof of their courage, she would respond to them...

response.speaker: Panuelle
response.text: But... I feared that she would not bestow her favor upon me, and so I brought a dragon scale with me.

response.speaker: Panuelle
response.text: Do you know about the giant dragon that suddenly emerged from the toytanium mines?

response.speaker: Panuelle
response.text: It flattened a great many homes and even mashed that mountain... Now, our venturers can no longer repair their boats or make tools there, and have had to change from whence they embark on their adventures...

response.speaker: Panuelle
response.text: That mountain is just over there, but nowadays, he's as broken as the Broken Sea itself.

response.speaker: Panuelle
response.text: We've constantly tried to chase the dragon away and defend our village!

response.speaker: Panuelle
response.text: Whenever it flew above our village, we would grab chairs, tables, forks, and spoons with which to chase it away.

choices.text: Seems as if you've succeeded thus far.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, whatever the case may be, at least that dragon hasn't come back to set fire to the village or roll over it or anything like that.

choices.text: Mini Durin's no evil dragon!

response.speaker: Panuelle
response.text: ...Is that so? In that case, his way of showing it is... most unexpected. Well, we couldn't understand what he was saying at the time anyway, so all we could do was chase him off.

response.speaker: Panuelle
response.text: When he left, he left behind a scale... I believed that it could prove my courage, and my neighbors thought so too.

response.speaker: Panuelle
response.text: And when I put the scale before the statue of the goddess, it began to glow with an awesome light!

response.speaker: Panuelle
response.text: I thought that this meant the goddess acknowledged my wish and was about to grant it.

response.speaker: Panuelle
response.text: But Chauvigne did not change. He still refused to come out of that pot, and he remains as upset as ever.

response.speaker: Panuelle
response.text: He even advised me to become a venturer and go on a long journey with him... No way am I doing that!

choices.text: Wait, come out of what "pot" now?

response.speaker: Panuelle
response.text: That's right. Chauvigne is presently a flower in a pot.

response.speaker: Panuelle
response.text: I mean, that's pretty alright, isn't it? He can live next to the tree, and I can take care of him, water him, drink tea, and sing for him.

response.speaker: Panuelle
response.text: But he always says that no matter where he goes, he must be sure of his place, something he learned from his venturing... and that pot is his place.

response.speaker: Panuelle
response.text: Coax and cajole as I might, I can't get him out of that pot... The goddess didn't make my wish come true, and I don't know what the matter is...

response.speaker: Panuelle
response.text: Ah, sorry for going on and on like that. Must've taken up quite a bit of your time there.

response.speaker: Panuelle
response.text: The Whispering Isle is that way. Perhaps the goddess will be more willing to hear your wish.

choices.text: It almost sounds like he's some sort of "potted" flower.
He just wants to be friends with everyone.
We should prepare a few utensils ourselves!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, it's not like that dragon's made of bread or butter or something. Forks and spoons wouldn't do squat to it!

choices.text: So, is there such a place to hang the lamp?
Paimon, fly that lamp way way up, would you?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And how long is Paimon supposed to stay up there, huh? We don't even know what the ideal elevation is — it's not like we can take measurements every few meters or something!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ugh... If only there really was a hook in the sky for us to hang that lamp on...

choices.text: Err... Okay, so what do we do now?
